Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, arrived in Tehran on Monday. Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi is accompanying him on the trip to the Iranian capital. The Pakistani army issued a statement saying that this senior military commander's visit to Tehran "will focus on Islamabad's efforts to promote regional peace and stability, and negotiations with Iranian officials on strengthening peace efforts and finding a peaceful, sustainable, and comprehensive solution to resolve Middle East conflicts." IRIB News reported that Asim Munir will meet with senior officials of the Islamic Republic. @VahidOOnLineReuters, citing several Pakistani officials, reported that Asim Munir, Pakistan's army chief, spoke by phone with Donald Trump last week before his trip to Tehran. Three Pakistani sources told Reuters that the call took place a few days before Munir was expected to travel to Tehran on Monday for talks with Islamic Republic officials. According to Reuters, this previously unreported call took place at a time when the US has announced it will impose broad economic sanctions against the Islamic Republic and its trading partners. The report also stated that Pakistan's army chief is expected to meet on Monday with people close to Mojtaba Khamenei. Reuters wrote that tensions between the US and the Islamic Republic are expected to be one of the main topics of this visit. Another source in the Pakistani government also said: "Munir is also expected to discuss the recent attacks by the Islamic Republic-affiliated Houthis on Saudi Arabia, Pakistan's ally." @VahidOOnLineIsmail Baghaei, the spokesman for the Islamic Republic's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, announced on Monday that Badr al-Busaidi, Oman's Minister of Foreign Affairs, will travel to Tehran on Tuesday. According to IRIB News, Baghaei told reporters that Busaidi will meet with Abbas Araghchi, the Islamic Republic's Foreign Minister, in Tehran. Following the US and Israeli attack and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic has begun negotiations with Oman to define a new legal regime for the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran, Muscat, and Doha report progress in these negotiations; however, US President Donald Trump threatened last week that he would bomb Oman if it obstructs the path of a "deal" between Tehran and Washington. Al-Busaidi mediated two rounds of negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the United States last year. Both rounds ended without results and with US and Israeli attacks on Iran. @VahidOOnLine📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [VahidOnline] 'Atousa Jafari', a 27-year-old woman from Sanandaj, was murdered with knife…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

'Atousa Jafari', a 27-year-old woman from Sanandaj, was murdered with knife blows in front of her family home on Sunday, August 23, 2026. Local media and the Kurdistan Human Rights Network have reported that Atousa Jafari was attacked and killed with multiple knife blows while leaving her house and before getting into her car to go to work. According to these reports, the perpetrator of the murder was Atousa Jafari's husband or ex-husband. Local sources have reported that she was killed with eight knife blows. Different accounts have been published about Atousa Jafari's marital status at the time of the murder. The Kurdistan Human Rights Network reported that she had separated from her husband two years ago and was living with her mother, but local media have written that Atousa had been referring to court over the past three years to separate from her husband, and her divorce request was not accepted. According to local sources, Atousa Jafari had been subjected to violence, beatings, and threats by her husband many times during this period. Once, as a result of the beatings, her arm was broken. The Kurdistan Human Rights Network wrote that Atousa Jafari was a postal office employee, held a master's degree in criminal law, and was an instructor and referee in the sport of 'Kung Fu Toa'. This is the second reported case of femicide in Kurdistan within a few days. On August 20, 2026, 'Latifeh Mohammadzadeh', a 49-year-old woman from Saqqez, was also murdered with knife blows by her ex-husband on one of the rural roads of that county. @VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [VahidOnline] The judiciary of the Islamic Republic has announced the execution of "Majid…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

The judiciary of the Islamic Republic has announced the execution of "Majid Adineh," another detainee from the protests of Dey 1404 (January 2026) in Karaj. According to a Tasnim report citing the judiciary, the sentence was carried out on the morning of Monday, Shahrivar 1, 1405 (August 23, 2026). Majid Adineh had been arrested on Dey 19, 1404 (January 9, 2026) in the Mohammadshahr area of Karaj. Judicial officials have claimed that at the time of his arrest, he was carrying a semi-automatic pistol, three magazines, 30 rounds of ammunition, two electric stun guns, two canisters of tear gas, a cordless saw, and a bottle of gasoline. The judiciary has described the Dey protests, according to the Islamic Republic's official narrative, as a "coup" and accused Adineh of cooperating with the United States, Israel, and what it called "hostile groups." The Revolutionary Court of Karaj had sentenced him to death and confiscation of assets on charges of "moharebeh (enmity against God) through intentional arson" under the so-called law on "aggravating punishment for espionage and cooperation with the Zionist regime and hostile countries." No information has been published about Adineh's access to a lawyer of his choice, the judicial process, the timing of the trial, or how his statements were obtained. The execution of Majid Adineh follows the ongoing implementation of death sentences against detainees from the Dey protests. On Mordad 21, 1405 (August 12, 2026), more than 30 countries issued a joint statement condemning the continued issuance and execution of death sentences against Iranian protesters as a tool to "silence the voices of opponents." Amnesty International has also reported that the Islamic Republic executed at least 2,159 people in 2025. @VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline
